The Command (R62)

Region (English scoring-table region): Rahen.

1444 starting country: The Command (R62)

One-line conclusion: The Command is an already-running continental war machine. Choose campaigns in the war room, balance six Commands, maintain the anti-magic Korashi reserve, and turn a three-way military alliance into a modern empire ruling Haless.

Narrative: Extremely high | Mission-tree length: Extremely long (215 direct missions in the current local script) | Mission-tree update: Locally verified for v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Extremely high | Waiting: High | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion capacity: Extremely high

Identity and History

The Command (R62) is a directly selectable hobgoblin military state in 1444. Its capital is Shamakhad, its primary culture is Wolf Hobgoblin, and it follows the Godlost faith. Moguwon Wolfborn rules with 5/5/6 ability; Barugi Lionborn and Kitokan Boarborn represent the other two core Commands' military power. [Local historical script]

The English Wiki supplies the longer formation story: between 1136 and 1392, an older tribal society was gradually replaced by a purely military hierarchy. By the fourteenth century the tribes had consolidated into the Wolf, Boar, and Lion Commands. In 1392 the three Commands ended their internal fighting and formed the Great Command; its second Grand Marshal, Moguwon Wolfborn, invaded Shamakhad in 1431, and after conquering Sil in 1435 the alliance formally regarded itself as an empire. [Wiki material]

The official dev diary describes hobgoblins moving south from the Jade Mines and defeating northern Raheni states. Earlier, they had taken the Jade Mines from dwarves and turned them into an unbreakable mountain base for the Lion Command. The Command is not a single kingdom but a military alliance of three Commands, whose supreme commander must keep all three obedient through the war room. [Official dev diary]

Anti-magic comes from collective memory. The dev diary says hobgoblin tribes were once ruled by shamans; after ordinary people overthrew them, magic became an institutional object of fear. The state therefore uses Korashi to make shackles that suppress spellcasters. This is not merely a strong army: war discipline, anti-magic, and rigid hierarchy are the state itself. [Official dev diary] [Local mechanics]

National Story and Campaign Arc

The first half of the campaign organises the interior: end the opening unrest, settle the Jade Mine subject states, rebuild the three Commands, and resettle Lion Command people on the surface. The war room then divides expansion into 25 regional campaigns. Each choice opens a small mission chain for that direction at the top of the tree. [Local missions] [Official dev diary]

As conquest succeeds, the old alliance becomes insufficient. The Command establishes the Tiger, Elephant, and Dragon Commands to administer Rahen, southern Haless, and Yanshen, while promoting “Wuhyun” identity among conquered humans. Humans who accept hobgoblin culture and Command order can enter the state system. The later story therefore changes from winning wars to deciding who may share the empire and who must obey. [Local missions] [Official dev diary]

Core Mechanics

War room and 25 campaigns. The war room is the expansion menu, not a decorative event. Campaign choice dynamically opens regional missions requiring armies, key holdings, and conquest. The 215 direct missions are therefore a modular continental war rather than a fixed left-to-right checklist. [Local missions] [Official dev diary]

Six Commands. Wolf, Boar, and Lion participate in politics as estates and factions from the start; the later Tiger, Elephant, and Dragon Commands organise newly conquered regions. Loyalty, privileges, generals, and government reforms decide whether the empire remains unified. The three new Commands are excluded from full power for a long time, driving the institutional conflict toward the Great Insubordination civil war. [Local missions] [Local disasters]

Korashi and the Rise of the Shamans. The dedicated resource begins at roughly 41, is capped at 100, and naturally declines. High reserves reduce army maintenance and stability costs; exhaustion triggers the Rise of the Shamans, bringing unrest, morale penalties, and rebel states. As the realm grows, suppressing magic consumes more resources and attention. [Local mechanics] [Local disasters]

Wuhyunisation and imperial governance. Missions turn some humans into Wuhyun culture and borrow Raheni offices and Yansheni eunuch institutions to build an administrative machine beyond the original alliance. This is a powerful integration route, but not an equality route: conquered people must accept the Command's definition of a respectable identity. [Local missions] [Official dev diary]

Slave states and the Jade frontier. Thunderfist, Bloodsong, Blackstep, and Stolen Gem are subject states handling enforcement, vanguards, and mine administration. Missions can also turn the Jade Mines into the Jade Frontier. These subjects relieve overextension and spread the front, but require simultaneous management of loyalty, migration, cultural change, and core territory. [Local diplomatic scripts] [Local missions]

Phased Play

Opening organisation: You have an unusually strong base, but the first goal is not a thoughtless multi-front war. Handle unrest, mine subjects, the three armies, and Korashi income so the war room can function.

Regional campaigns: Choose campaigns around truces, aggressive expansion, and resources. The Xiadao direction can help relieve early Korashi pressure; advances into Rahen, Yanshen, and southern Haless should remain reasonably balanced to prepare the three new Commands and the Great Insubordination.

Imperial restructuring: New Commands, Wuhyunisation, and administrative reform arrive together. The difficulty is no longer defeating neighbours; it is the interaction of mission gates, estate loyalty, governing capacity, resource drain, and multi-front tempo.

Disasters and endgame: The Great Insubordination makes the Tiger, Elephant, and Dragon Commands revolt; the Rise of the Shamans punishes poor Korashi management. After surviving, missions require all campaigns completed and at least 350 Wuhyun provinces in Rahen, Yanshen, and southern Haless.

Mission Future and Endgame

The Command has no fixed formation country and does not need to change Tag. The final “X Edict” mission triggers a country-renaming event that can display “Supreme Command,” while the Tag remains R62. This is a mission future after continental conquest and state transformation, not an established fact in 1444. [Local missions] [Local localisation]

Official future material for the associated setting gives another outcome: in the Victoria 3 era, the Command collapses during the Great Insubordination after the Rending of Realms. That confirms it is not an eternal victor in the wider setting, but cannot be projected backward as an inevitable EU4 campaign failure. [Official cross-setting material]

The English Wiki provides a longer setting chronology: the Rending, prolonged wars, and imbalance between old and new Commands eventually ignite the Great Insubordination; central authority keeps dissolving, and by 1835 the army's rank and file overthrow the last Grand Marshal, dissolve the old Commands, and create a new civil state. This is a setting future that a player can rewrite through the EU4 mission line. [Wiki material]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 100/100 | Autocracy 100/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 50/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; theme intensity 78/100) | Pluralism 25/100.

The v2.1 value score is Evil (15/100), with a stable trajectory. Slave subjects, bound spellcasters, institutionalised anti-magic persecution, and forced identity remaking are the principal negatives; continental conquest is not counted a second time merely because it is conquest.

This is for players who enjoy a strong opening, an exceptionally long tree, continuous wars, dynamic campaign choice, estate politics, and major civil wars. Avoid it if you want peaceful development, dislike late-game map checklists, reject assimilation and slavery narratives, or do not want to manage several resources and disasters. [Local scripts]

Community Experience

[Community view] A 2023 beginner guide argues that Korashi determines early campaign order and that the Great Insubordination requires advance planning for the three new Commands, forts, and allies. Its specific numbers are old-version experience and do not override the current script.

[Community view] A 2025 discussion treats the Command both as Haless's endgame boss and as the centre of a regional design dispute: supporters like the sustained threat and imperial-collapse story, while critics say other Halessi countries are forced to plan their entire campaigns around it. This describes player experience, not current AI strength.

Evidence Boundary

This article targets the local base game and localisation supporting v1.37.5.0, checked on 16 September 2026. Tag, Chinese name, 1444 identity, 215 direct missions, six Commands, Korashi, the two disasters, and the endgame rename come from local files.

The English Wiki's The Command page was read from the offline snapshot (page_id=1253, revision_id=30147). Only opening history and institutions are used here; post-1445 chronology is explicitly setting future. The offline Wiki tool directory was rechecked on 26 September 2026 and reported health status ok. Reddit is used only for official design context and two player experiences; the full source list is in the source receipt. [Wiki material] [Community views]

Full inherited research references and version boundaries: original Chinese evidence record.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

The Command (R62) — Hobgoblin Ideas

Traditions: Hobgoblin Traditions

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +15%; global_autonomy：-0.05%.

Idea 1: An Empire Forged in Blood

In the aftermath of our invasion of northern Rahen, we had to quickly adapt our administration to accommodate the new territories. Many local leaders organised resistance against our rule, which weakened our control over the conquered lands. In response we hunted them down and executed them. We ensured that they were replaced with weaker willed locals. These meek rulers would lead by example. Under the watchful eye of hobgoblin garrisons they greatly weakened any resistance to our rule. It was through these strict measures that newly conquered peoples and lands could be quickly incorporated into our Great Command as we marched upon Haless.

Effects: Core-creation cost: -15%.

Idea 2: Modern Drill Techniques

Through many generations we have developed traditional techniques of drilling our armies. While these techniques had been adequate for border protection and the conquest of the Jade Mines, our expansion into northern Haless introduced us to several new enemies. This kick-started the development of modernised drills. The two main drills were those developed by the Wolf Command, which centered around cavalry flanking maneuvers, and those developed by the Boar command, which centered around massed infantry. The latter of the two would prove a very effective baseline for later firearm drills.

Effects: Discipline: +5%; Army Drill Gain Modifier: +25%.

Idea 3: Warforged Society

Constant warfare both within and outside of the Jade Mines has pushed hobgoblin society into ever greater centralisation and militarisation in the form of various Commands, culminating in the founding of the Great Command in 1391 AA. This has led to hobgoblin society becoming an incredibly well oiled machine capable of supplying vast armies with extreme efficiency, with almost every household capable of producing weapons, uniforms and soldiers for the Great Command’s endless campaigns. This has resulted in a civil society that is completely integrated into the purpose of the state: War.

Effects: Army maintenance modifier: -10%.

Idea 4: Honourable Service

Honour is a core pillar of our culture. And honour is kept through loyalty. No good hobgoblin would even consider betraying their duty to their family and Command and lose their honour. A hobgoblin without honour loses their family, their position, their very place in society. They are removed from all the things that give meaning to life and thus often end up with two options, suicide or exile. Suicide is the preferred choice for those who have dishonoured themselves, for such is the weight of our honour. No secrets are spilled.

Effects: global_spy_defence：+25%.

Idea 5: Expanded Ninyu Kikun

As the armies of the Wolf, Boar and Lion grew in size and strength, various Grand Marshals of the Great Command sought to expand the forces directly controlled by them beyond the enslaved Zanyu Kikun. This led to the creation and steady expansion of the Ninyu Kikun, the combined army, which answered only to the Grand Marshal. This force would systematically recruit the most disciplined soldiers and most accomplished commanders into the service of the Grand Marshal, eventually forming the most formidable army of the Command. The Ninyu Kikun would be the first of the armies to adopt artillery into their formations, crushing enemy defences and opposition while paving the way for the artillery innovations of the Dragon Command. The existence of the Ninyu Kikun also served to increase the authority and control of the Grand Marshal within the military structures of the Command and by extension their authority over the lesser Marshals.

Effects: Land force limit modifier: +25%.

Idea 6: Military Education

Hobgoblin military education begins in the family, with grandfathers and fathers beginning the process of passing down their martial skills to their sons from the age of 8. Years of training from a young age form the foundation that a young hobgoblin builds upon through their introduction into larger military divisions, such as a senun, banner, or ten, regiment. It is here that a hobgoblin has the opportunity to distinguish themselves on the battlefield, potentially earning an exaltation from a superior officer. A hobgoblin soldier who earns themselves an exaltation is given an advanced military education and promoted to captain, regardless of their clan’s status. The system of exaltations ensures that the officer corps of the Command has greater pools of talents to draw upon than most states on Halann and prevents the elite clans from monopolising leadership positions.

Effects: Leaders without upkeep: +1; General cost: -20%.

Idea 7: The Six Command System

Our expansion outside of Shamakhad began to strain the administration due to the lack of loyal and honourable hobgoblins to govern our newly conquered lands. This led to our Grand Marshal dividing the three original Commands into the Tiger, Elephant and Dragon commands, who would found war camps and settle in the lands outside of Shamakhad. The influx of our people into the distant territories allowed for the expansion and spread of hobgoblin garrisons, easing the pressure on our central administration and ensuring that our Great Command could govern the dishonourable peoples of Haless with greater efficiency than before.

Effects: Governing Capacity Modifier: +20%.

Ambition: Hobgoblin Ambition

Effects: Army tradition: +1.
